query: A Lease by the Harbour The lease comes with a brass key and a letter from a harbour landlord whose wife swears by your hair tonic. A crooked little shop, two rooms and a still, yours from the autumn if you sign on the last day. Nobody has ever offered you a door of your own before. Keep the key on a string round your neck You wear the key under your robes for the rest of the year. It's warm when you touch it, which is probably the hair tonic's doing. Write back about the drains The landlord's reply is two pages about the drains, which you read twice. An alchemist's shop lives or dies by its drains. This one, apparently, will live.
